title: This Bird Has a Harem of Husbands and Dad Hides the Chicks Under His Wings

scenes.text: In this bird, the female has the harem. And the dads do all the work.
The jacana. Huge, spread-out toes let it walk across floating lily pads without sinking.
One female can control three or four males, and each male gets his own nest.
She defends the whole territory. He sits on the eggs for about three weeks.
When danger comes, dad tucks the chicks under his wings and runs.
Legs dangling out of his feathers, he carries them to safety. Polyandry, at its best.

description:
Jacanas flip the usual bird family roles. Females hold large territories and mate with several males, each of which incubates his own clutch for about three weeks and guards the chicks. Their extra-long toes spread their weight across floating plants, and when threatened a male can tuck chicks under his wings and carry them away.
Which animal dad deserves a medal? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: MOM HAS A HAREM OF DADS
first_comment: Eight jacana species exist, and the lesser jacana is the monogamous exception where both parents share the work. Which bird dad impressed you most?
